## Version control

Git was initialised on 2026-10-06, after this document was first written, in
`health-data-distributions`, `agreekit`, and `spo2-skin-tone` (branch `main`,
no remote). Each has a single initial commit holding the state this document
describes, so there is no earlier history to recover from. The local
copy of `validation-study-designer` is not a git repository and was left
alone: its history lives in its GitHub repository, and it should be cloned

folder.

## Test baseline (verified)

```
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q                  65 passed, 1 skipped
.venv/Scripts/python pipelines/validate.py         ok
.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check --line-length 110 .    All checks passed!
```

The one skip is deliberate: a proportions-only test skipping the one
`moments` source among the transcribed skin tone sources. Any failure is a
real regression.

Environment: `.venv` with numpy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.6, pillow 12.3.0, pytest
9.1.1, ruff 0.16.10. Use `.venv/Scripts/python`; `python3` on this machine is
the Windows Store stub and hangs. There is no `requirements.txt` yet.

## Process

Directive, implement, audit, mirroring the Sentinel and Pragma convention in
`C:\repos\volatility-underwriting`. Sentinel (Opus) writes directives and
audits; Pragma (Sonnet) implements. Specs are in `.claude/agents/`.

- Directives 01 to 05 are implemented, audited, and in `_completed/`. Each
  file carries its implementation report and audit.
- In practice this session, Pragma did directives 01 to 05's format and
  research work, and Sentinel did the paper reading, figure measurement, and
  most source entry directly, because the PDFs and images were in Sentinel's
  context. Those additions are recorded in the audits of directives 04 and 05
  and in the source files themselves, not as separate directives.
- What worked: Pragma refused to enter untraceable numbers, reported its own
  failing checks, and corrected two errors in Sentinel's directive 04.
  Every audit re-ran the checks and re-opened primary sources.
- What to watch: the web fetch tool summarises through a small model that
  invented statements twice. Numbers must come from the raw text of a source,
  never from a fetch summary or a search result.

## Things that are easy to get wrong

- **"Fitzpatrick type" means at least three different measurements** in these
  sources: self-reported sun reaction, an observer's rating of colour, and an
  instrument threshold. Self-report and dermatologist rating agree for 31% of
  the same people in SCIN. Never pool across them.
- **Question wording drives self-report.** Black respondents: 59.0% "none of
  the above" when offered sun-reaction options only; 48.4% Type VI on a
  six-type sun-reaction question; 71.1% Type VI when the options name a
  colour.
- **Raters disagree.** NHANES readers match on 61.6% of people; SCIN Monk
  annotator pools on 40.1%.
- **The published NHANES headline depends on an unstated rounding rule**
  (half-points rounded down). Rounding up moves Type III from 47.8% to 68.4%.
- **The clinic pulse and wearable resting heart rate are different
  quantities.** The page states both means and attributes the gap to nothing
  in particular.
- **Several papers' tables contain small internal inconsistencies.** They are
  recorded in caveats as printed, not corrected.

## The wider plan this belongs to

**`ROADMAP.md` at the repository root tracks every milestone and end point,
with status.** It is the running record; this section is a snapshot summary.

Later on 2026-10-06 the roadmap was rewritten around a north star: five tools
that together cover the work of validating a measurement of the human body
(plan, know what is normal, know the device, analyse, know the regulatory
bar), plus three case studies and a hub. Two of the five tools are new ideas
with no code. The headings below use the earlier project names; the roadmap
gives the mapping.

Four linked projects were agreed in this session. Only the first two have
code.

### `C:\repos\agreekit` — validation statistics toolkit (Project 5)

Python package for agreement statistics with repeated measures handled
properly. **44 tests pass** (about 30 seconds; includes simulation coverage
checks and 15 checks against numbers printed in Carkeet 2015 and Bland and
Altman 2007). Copies of its three source papers are in its own `raw/papers/`
(git-ignored; see its `PAPERS.md`). Own `.venv` with numpy, scipy, pandas.

- Has: bias and limits of agreement (exact intervals for one sample per
  subject, subject bootstrap otherwise), variance components and effective
  sample size, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, within-tolerance shares, error percentiles,
  equivalence test, categorical agreement for sleep stages (accuracy, kappa,
  per-class sensitivity, specificity, PPV; pooled or subject-averaged),
  methods-text generator.
- Its planned-precision functions match the Validation Study Designer's SciPy
  fixtures to 10 significant figures.
- Does not have: a check for error that varies across the measurement range
  (needed first for oximetry), the analytic repeated-measures interval (Zou
  2013), mixed-effects or Bayesian models, plots, time alignment for heart
  rate, any cross-check against R (R is not installed here; the published worked
  examples now stand in for one).
- Checking against Bland and Altman 2007 found that the subject labels in that
  paper's Table 1 are shifted by one row for subjects 6 to 8. Details are in
  agreekit's `PAPERS.md`.
- The name is a placeholder; PyPI availability was not checked.

### `C:\repos\spo2-skin-tone` — pulse oximeter accuracy by skin tone (Project 1)

One script only: `scripts/inventory.py`, an aggregate-only inventory of the
OpenOximetry download (masked paths, percentiles not extremes, cells under 5
suppressed). Tested on synthetic data, never run on the real data.

**Data handling rule, agreed with Ross:** PhysioNet's guidance says not to
use an AI service whose data handling cannot be verified, and this one
cannot. So Claude never reads subject-level OpenOximetry data. Claude writes
scripts; Ross runs them in his own terminal; only schemas and aggregates come
back. The planned location is `C:\data\openox\`, outside `C:\repos`. A folder
of that name exists; its contents were not inspected. The browser download
(3.2 GB) was in progress during the session and its completion was not
confirmed.

Still open before any analysis: the clearance question from the Designer's
`HANDOFF.md` section 7 (Monk skin tone notebooks written during Ross's Google
employment), and a pre-specified analysis plan.

The skin tone entry in this repository is directly relevant: it documents how
unreliable "Fitzpatrick V to VI" is as a recruitment criterion.

### `C:\repos\validation-study-designer` — existing, live site

Not changed this session. Agreed next addition: a repeated-measures module
(subjects by samples per subject, effective sample size), fed by agreekit's
variance components and by real values from the oximetry analysis.

### Change-point false-alarm benchmark (no folder yet)

Prompted by Lautman et al. 2026 (*JACC Case Reports*; a copy is held in this
repository's `raw/papers/` until that project has a folder): how often does a
healthy person's wearable data show a "coordinated step change"? Ross was
advised to start wearing the Garmin Instinct 2X Solar and Fitbit Inspire 3
together, with a confounder log, since baseline only accrues with calendar
time. Whether that has started is not known.

### Parked

Road-surface vibration map from a bike-mounted IMU; NHANES accelerometry
reference curves (now the `daily_activity` placeholder here); open sleep
staging benchmark; cycling durability modelling.
